#The Vault helper protocol

On this page

  • Frames
  • Requests and answers
  • Login steps
  • Idle deadline
  • Errors
  • The helper's identity at the server
  • Matching
  • Wren's side

Wren talks to its Vault helper, wren-vault, through two anonymous pipes: the helper's standard input carries the requests, its standard output the answers. The design is in bitwarden.md. The helper is a separate program under GPL-3.0-only, in its own repository; its README.md has the same description. This page and that README must stay equal: a change of the protocol changes both, and PROTOCOL_VERSION in src/vault/protocol.odin and in the helper.

The protocol is generic: accounts, logins and plain values. No type of the Bitwarden SDK crosses the pipe.

Version 3 (helper 0.3.0). Changes from version 2: new requests search and totp; fill takes the field totp; logins_for applies the rules StartsWith and Exact and the account's equivalent domains, its rows carry the match types equivalent, starts_with and exact, and its answer carries equivalent; the error no_totp.

Version 2 (helper 0.2.0) changed from version 1: the server choice is Wren's (the helper gets URLs as before); login carries code and provider instead of totp, and answers need_device_code; new requests login_api_key, logout, pin_set, pin_clear; unlock takes pin; hello takes idle_seconds and answers login and pin; the event locked.

#Frames

  • Each message is one frame: a 4-byte unsigned length, little-endian, then that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one object).
  • The length is from 1 to 1 048 576 (1 MiB). A frame outside these bounds ends the connection.
  • The helper answers each request, in the order of the requests. keepalive has no answer.
  • The helper writes nothing else on its standard output, and no value of the vault on its standard error.
  • The helper exits when its standard input closes, after it answers lock or logout, and at its idle deadline.

#Requests and answers

A request is {"id": <integer from 1>, "op": "<name>", ...fields}. The answer repeats the id:

  • success: {"id": n, "ok": true, ...fields}
  • failure: {"id": n, "ok": false, "error": "<code>", "message": "<sentence>"}

An event answers no request: {"id": 0, "ok": true, "event": "<name>"}.

#Login steps

  • provider is authenticator (an authenticator app's code; the default), email (a code by email) or device (the code of the server's new-device mail). providers lists the second steps of the account that the helper supports (authenticator, email); an account with none of them gets unsupported_two_factor.
  • A login with a second step is two requests or more. The first login (email and password) answers need_two_factor or need_device_code; the helper keeps the email, the password and the device identifier of that login. The second login carries the same email, the code and its provider: Wren sends the master password once. A failed second step forgets the kept password.
  • resend asks for a code again. With provider email, the helper asks the server to mail the two-step code and answers need_two_factor with email_sent true. With device, it sends the first step again and the server mails a new code. email_sent is also true when the email code is the account's only second step: the server mailed it.

#Idle deadline

hello's idle_seconds (0: none) is the helper's own lock. When no request (keepalive included) comes for that long, the helper writes the event locked and exits. Wren sends it its own idle time and a margin (vault.lock.idle_minutes × 60 + 120); Wren locks first, on its own timer, and sends a keepalive at most once a minute while the user is active.

#Errors

bad_request, bad_protocol, no_hello, bad_server, bad_credentials, unsupported_two_factor, unsupported_account, network, login_failed, no_account, bad_password, bad_pin, pin_reset, no_pin, no_state, locked, sync_failed, no_item, no_totp, decrypt, state_write, state_format. The helper's README says what each means.

#The helper's identity at the server

The helper sends its own token request (the SDK's sends the device type ChromeBrowser and one device identifier for every SDK user, and cannot carry the new-device code): client id web, device type 14 (UnknownBrowser), device name Wren, and a random device identifier made at the first login and kept in the state. The SDK's HTTP client gets the same device type (the Device-Type header). A renewal with an API key goes through the SDK and still names its fixed device; no new-device check applies to API keys.

#Matching

The helper selects the logins whose saved URI matches the page: Domain (the URI's host is the page's registrable domain or a subdomain of it: domain; or one of the domains the account makes equivalent to it, or a subdomain of one: equivalent; a page without a registrable domain uses Host), Host (same host and port), StartsWith (the page's address starts with the URI) and Exact (the page's address is the URI), both addresses as the URL standard serializes them. RegularExpression and Never match nothing. An item saved for https never matches an http page. The equivalent domains are the account's own groups and the server's global groups it did not exclude, from the last sync.

Wren checks every returned row again with its own Public Suffix List (src/vault/match.odin) on the blocking pool, before a surface shows it. An equivalent row stays only if the saved host's registrable domain is in the answer's equivalent. A row with a match type Wren does not know is dropped when the answer is read. A row that fails the check is zeroed and dropped. search rows are not checked: they fill only when the same item is also a checked row of the focused document (docs/bitwarden.md 3.5, rule 10).

#Wren's side

src/vault (no interface, no dependency on the browser):

FileWhat
protocol.odinThe requests, written into one buffer reserved large enough at once; the answers, decoded into owned values. Every string that can hold a value is zeroed before it is freed.
transport.odin, process.odinThe helper as a child process: a reader thread starts it, reads and decodes frames and posts each answer to the loop; a writer thread writes the queued frames in order and zeroes each. The loop thread never blocks on the helper.
vault.odinThe one state of the Vault, the requests and their deadlines (vault.request.timeout_ms), the three sets of rows (the tab's document, the focused frame's document, the palette's search), the fill's ticket, the copies, the idle and sync timers, the blocking jobs (locating the helper, the account file, the check of the rows, the join of an ended helper).
match.odinWren's match check.
settings.odinThe vault.* preferences and the server addresses (US, EU, self-hosted).
